sources.label: GHSL GHS-POP R2023A
sources.notes: Source-native five-year global estimate rasters from 1975 to 2020 and distinct 2025/2030 projection rasters are acquired for conservative one-degree display aggregation. Source totals and outside-grid residuals are preserved; grid bins are never assigned to historical polities or silently rebased to World Bank totals.

sources.label: WorldPop Global2 R2025A v1
sources.notes: Separate annual modeled reconstruction, constrained to UN WPP 2024 January 1 national totals; it must not be spliced into GHSL or World Bank. The official 2020 global BigTIFF is acquired and SHA-256 pinned. A review-only center-bin pass conserves 7,849,969,310.541 modeled people over 15,432 covered one-degree bins (18 valid-zero bins), with zero outside-grid count and a 0.0000038-person floating residual. The official hub calls datasets CC BY 4.0, while WorldPop's general terms note ODbL for outputs derived from Microsoft layers; this release statement explicitly documents Microsoft Building Footprints input. Exact derivative applicability must be resolved before publication.

sources.label: Cliopatria
sources.notes: Pinned v0.2.0 archive acquired and profiled: 13,765 rows, including 13,380 POLITY and 385 RELATION records. Release r6 publishes 36 simplified POLITY-only context snapshots; RELATION is excluded and no feature contributes to population accounting. Reconciliation v1 covers all 28 bounded 1500 CE overlap candidates: 8 are source-declared Components/MemberOf hierarchies rendered with composite outlines, while 20 remain visibly unresolved. Six source year-zero endpoints remain quarantined; no snapshot samples source year zero.

sources.label: HYDE 3.5
sources.notes: The official README and one 10,000 BCE baseline population bundle were acquired through the provider's normal browser flow. The sample contains five 5-arc-minute grids; the population-count grid has 4,487,003.996 modeled inhabitants across 2,215,829 non-NODATA cells. Nothing is published: the archive License.txt says CC BY-NC 4.0 while the README says CC BY 3.0, and the README simultaneously mentions a 2025 extension and a coverage sentence ending in 2023. Provider clarification, masks, scenario samples, and mass reconciliation remain required.

sources.label: UN World Population Prospects 2024
sources.notes: Official medium demographic-indicators CSV acquired, profiled, and published as a separate source-native metric: 237 Country/Area series annually from 1950 through 2100. The official download page establishes that TPopulation1July is in thousands and licenses the material under CC BY 3.0 IGO. Atlas converts exactly to people, excludes aggregate and 2101 boundary rows, marks 1950-2023 estimates versus 2024-2100 Medium projections, preserves the World rounding residual, and does not splice the series into World Bank population.

sources.label: World Bank World Development Indicators
sources.coverage_start: 1960 CE for population and life expectancy; 1990 CE for electricity
sources.coverage_end: 2025 CE for population; 2024 CE for electricity
sources.notes: API rows and metadata acquired/profiled for the full MVP windows. The app publishes annual population for 1960-2025, electricity for 1990-2024, and life expectancy for 1960-2024. Life expectancy is territorial context, not an individual distribution. Aggregates are excluded; WLD is reference-only and the residual is explicit. See data/registry/source-lock.json.

sources.label: World Bank World Development Indicators — economics
sources.notes: The r7 Atlas map retains its July 2026 GDP-per-capita release. Thirteen additional indicator responses and country metadata from the October 2026 update are pinned separately in economic-source-lock.json and published as source-native tables in r9. They are not cross-release spliced or assigned to historical borders.

sources.label: Maddison Project Database 2023
sources.coverage_start: 1 CE (14 supports with GDP per capita; 10000 BCE not covered)
sources.notes: The official 2023 workbook was acquired via the publisher-linked Dataverse file endpoint on 2026-10-24. Its Full data sheet supplies GDP per capita in 2011 international dollars; its Sources and Maddison original sources sheets are retained in the r9 dataset as candidate original-paper references. The source values are published as a separate source-native table, without a border join, global mean, or graphical claim of per-row paper provenance.

sources.label: World Inequality Database
sources.candidate_release: Current downloadable WID series, version not pinned
sources.notes: WID is a priority candidate for income and wealth shares, quantiles, and national income. Its concepts, population units, quality grades, and source methods cannot be collapsed into a World Bank Gini row or reused under a report-level license. No WID data is claimed acquired or published.

sources.label: Seshat Global History Databank
sources.coverage_start: source-coded -13600 in TSDat123; variable-specific and not yet date-normalized
sources.notes: The public Equinox v1 Zenodo archive and metadata are pinned. The CanonDat sheet contains 395 Polity Population rows over 275 PolID values; 178 rows have no Date.From and 48 have textual Value.From. None of those 275 PolIDs exactly matches the 426 distinct Cliopatria SeshatID values, so no population-to-border join is published. Derived/imputed Scale_MI values are not treated as source-native population observations. This is a historical research sample, not complete global coverage.

sources.label: V-Dem
sources.coverage_start: 1789 CE for the selected suffrage candidate; variable-specific
sources.notes: The provider-owned v16 RData package, official v16 codebook, and release metadata are pinned. The first candidate variable is v2x_suffr, a de-jure adult-citizen suffrage share; it is not yet published because the large RData object and entity support still require a reproducible adapter audit. No cross-release splicing or Atlas-authored democracy score is allowed.

sources.label: Clio Infra
sources.notes: The Total Population compact workbook is now pinned for review: 3,221 unique country/year rows, 190 country codes, sparse exact dates from 1500 to 2000, with only 70 rows in 1500. The portal describes modern 2012 boundaries and cites multiple underlying authors. The workbook metadata gives a dataset-level citation but no row-level source sheet. Per-artifact reuse terms, exact units, underlying citations, and geographic crosswalk must be resolved before publication. Earlier GDP, conflict, and institutional workbooks are also pinned candidates. An early catalog date does not imply dense or global coverage.

sources.label: UCDP
sources.coverage_start: 1946 CE for conflict-years; 1989 CE for georeferenced events
sources.notes: UCDP GED 26.1 (event records, 1989–2025), UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset 26.1 (conflict-years, 1946–2025), and both codebooks are pinned. They remain separate products: event locations, conflict parties, and territorial context are not interchangeable, and no conflict exposure prevalence is inferred.

sources.label: Our World in Data life expectancy
sources.notes: Do not confuse processed data rights with visualization software rights.

sources.label: CShapes 2.0
sources.notes: Official CShapes 2.0 Gleditsch-Ward GeoJSON and codebook are pinned and profiled for comparison only: 710 dated geometry features, including 11 invalid geometries. CShapes maps independent states and dependent territories from 1886-2019, but is an international-system coding universe rather than a universal map of political belonging. The downloaded GeoJSON lacks several codebook fields needed for defensible dependency and undefined-border rendering, and its CC BY-NC-SA terms require a product-use decision before publication.

sources.label: Modelski Ancient v2
sources.notes: Pinned Figshare V2 CSV: 154 cities, 41 sparse exact dates from 3700 BCE to 1000 CE, and 621 published estimates. Coordinates and source certainty codes are preserved. Release r6 adds canonical place links from the versioned reconciliation set while keeping every population estimate source-native. The layer is not a complete population surface or denominator.

sources.label: World Historical Gazetteer
sources.notes: Useful for historically scoped names, place identifiers, and reconciliation. It aggregates many licenses and is not a single globally reusable border dataset.

sources.label: Chandler v2
sources.notes: Audited fixture has 1,597 city rows, 806 sparse source-date columns, and 9,438 populated cells. Reconciliation v1 covers all 353 candidates: 336 accepted place links, 15 rejected distant homonyms, and 2 unresolved coordinate-only identities. Links never merge population values. Two Chandler cells and the multiple-source disagreement presentation remain unresolved.

sources.label: Modelski Modern v2
sources.notes: Audited fixture has 293 city rows and 293 positive estimates at 2000 CE. Reconciliation v1 records 336 accepted place links, 15 rejected distant homonyms, and 2 unresolved coordinate-only identities across all three series. The source observations remain separate until same-date disagreements have a truthful presentation.

sources.label: Pleiades
sources.notes: Authoritative open ancient-place gazetteer for names and locations, including explicitly unlocated places. It is not a polity-border source.

sources.label: U.S. Census historical world population
sources.license: U.S. government public data; underlying estimates attributed
sources.notes: Release r2 publishes all 39 table dates. Summary lower/upper values are preserved as source-disagreement ranges, not confidence intervals. Values have world support only and are never assigned to Cliopatria polities.

sources.label: Natural Earth 5.1.2
sources.notes: v5.1.2 1:110m admin-0 GeoJSON acquired for display only; checksum is pinned in data/registry/source-lock.json. Modern coastline remains an explicit approximation in deep-time mode.
